newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CURCIC'S VILLA FUTURE REMAINS IN DOUBT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CURCIC'S VILLA FUTURE REMAINS IN DOUBT.

text.p: The future of Aston Villa's record signing Sasa Curcic was thrown into further doubt on Monday following his omission from the squad for Tuesday's F.A. Cup clash at Notts County despite a lengthy injury list.

Villa manager Brian Little decided to leave his four million pounds ($6.7 million) buy kicking his heels on the sidelines for the second successive match after Cucic's outburst in which he claimed that "leaving Bolton Wanderers was the biggest mistake of my life."
Little had initially been considering recalling Curcic but said his approach to Monday's training session convinced him the player was not in the right frame of mind to rate a comeback.
Little was planning talks with Curcic later this week, and, publicly at least, was optimistic the problem could be resolved.

But realistically it was looking increasingly unlikely the future of the Yugoslav international remained at Villa Park -- with Leeds believed to be interested in signing Curcic should he become available
Little said: "Everyone knows he apologised last week for what he said but he is still not happy. As a manger you look at people and get body language messages from them.
"I've got an unhappy player and I don't need an unhappy player in the team at the moment so I won't pick him. I owe it to the other players to give them an opportunity to play in the team.
"Sasa wants to have a chat with me but he wants his advisors with him to help him say whatever needs to be said in the right way.

"I'll be concentrating on the game with Notts County, but I'll speak to him after that and hopefully we can resolve this situation by the end of the week. But as to the outcome, I don't know what tomorrow will bring."
Curcic, unhappy at failing to command a regular place, was not in the squad despite injuries to Ian Taylor, Mark Draper, Fernando Nelson and Dwight Yorke.
